_comment: Answer-quality cases for ask_mailbox and summarize_thread over the synthetic baseline mailbox (indexer/tests/baseline/corpus.py). A case id starts with its tool's short name (ask-, summarize-); a summarize_thread case names a baseline thread ID directly (nothing is embedded) and its evidence must be in that thread (the per-tool argument rules are in cases.py). Synthetic data only: never add a case built from a real mailbox. Message refs 'tNN.M' mean 'tNN.M@baseline.example'; thread refs 'tNN' mean the thread rooted at 'tNN.1@baseline.example'. required_evidence is a list of groups: every group is required and any one ref inside a group satisfies it. Each expected fact lists the message refs and a short verbatim excerpt of the indexed text that establishes it; make baseline checks each excerpt is in that message's indexed text, so references stay independent of what the system retrieves. deterministic.must_include is a list of groups of acceptable spellings (every group required, any spelling in a group satisfies it, case-insensitive substring of the answer). must_include checks that a value is present, not that the answer asserts it: an answer that names the value only to deny or correct it still passes, so correctness needs the judge. must_not_include lists strings no answer may contain. criteria say which rubric dimensions apply; the judge may not mark an applicable one not_applicable. held_out must equal tests/agent_metrics.py is_held_out(id); never tune against held-out cases. review records that the expected facts were drafted with AI from the synthetic corpus and await owner verification.
